home.faqSubtitle: Everything you need to know about Trader Master and how it works.
home.faq1A: Trader Master is an AI-powered Forex intelligence platform built exclusively for MT5 traders. It offers three core tools — AI Trade (chart analysis), AI Chat (market assistant), and AI Strategy (strategy generation) — all powered by proprietary visual analytics and institutional data feeds.
home.faq2Q: Do I need an MT5 account to use Trader Master?
home.faq2A: While you can explore the platform without one, linking your Avatrade MT5 account unlocks the full credit system. Your trading activity on Avatrade automatically replenishes your AI analysis credits.
home.faq3Q: How does the credit system work?
home.faq3A: Every AI interaction (chart analysis, chat query, strategy generation) costs credits. You earn credits by trading on your linked Avatrade account — each completed trade cycle automatically replenishes your balance. No subscription or upfront payment required.
home.faq4Q: Is my trading data safe with Trader Master?
home.faq4A: Absolutely. Trader Master never accesses your brokerage account directly, does not hold client deposits, and does not execute trades on your behalf. We are a technology and research platform — not a broker. Your data is protected with industry-standard encryption and security measures.
home.faq5Q: What currency pairs and markets are supported?
home.faq5A: Trader Master supports 50+ currency pairs including all major, minor, and exotic Forex pairs, plus commodities (Gold, Silver, Oil) and global indices (US30, NAS100, etc.). Market data is sourced from institutional feeds for analytical accuracy.
home.faq6Q: Is Trader Master a broker or financial advisor?
home.faq6A: No. Trader Master operates exclusively as an AI technology and market research platform. We are not a registered broker-dealer, financial custodian, or investment advisor. All analysis is for informational and educational purposes only.
home.faq7Q: How accurate is the AI chart analysis?
home.faq7A: Our AI models are trained on extensive historical market data and continuously refined. While no analysis tool can guarantee accuracy, Trader Master identifies structure, key levels, patterns, and risk/reward math that professional traders rely on daily. Always validate AI insights with your own analysis.
home.faq8Q: Can I use Trader Master on my phone?
home.faq8A: Yes. Trader Master is a web-based platform accessible from any modern browser on desktop, tablet, or mobile. No app download is required — simply visit the website and log in to access all features.

pastTradeFaq.subtitle: Everything you need to know about Past Trade Analyzer.
pastTradeFaq.a1: Past Trade Analyzer is an AI-powered trade review feature that analyzes completed trades and provides structured feedback on execution, market context, risk management, and potential mistakes.
pastTradeFaq.a2: You can upload a screenshot of a completed trade or provide the supported trade information required by the analyzer. The clearer and more complete the information, the more useful the analysis can be.
pastTradeFaq.a3:
The analyzer can review areas such as:
• Entry and exit
• Market structure
• Price action
• Key levels
• Stop-loss and take-profit
• Risk/reward
• Trade outcome
• Execution quality
pastTradeFaq.q4: Can it tell me why I lost a trade?
pastTradeFaq.a4: It can identify potential factors that may have contributed to the trade outcome, such as premature entries, weak confirmation, poor risk/reward, stop placement, or other execution issues visible in the available trade information.
pastTradeFaq.a5: Yes. Reviewing winning trades can be just as useful as reviewing losing ones. It can help you understand what elements of your execution and setup worked well.
pastTradeFaq.q6: Does Past Trade Analyzer automatically know my trading strategy?
pastTradeFaq.a6: Not necessarily. The analysis is based on the information available from your trade and chart. For more meaningful comparisons, you should use your own strategy rules and trading context where the product supports them.
pastTradeFaq.q7: Can it identify repeated trading mistakes?
pastTradeFaq.a7: A single trade can reveal an issue, but repeated trade reviews are much more useful for identifying recurring patterns in your execution.
pastTradeFaq.q8: Does it give me a trading signal for my next trade?
pastTradeFaq.a8: Past Trade Analyzer is primarily a review and learning tool. Its purpose is to analyze completed trades and provide feedback, rather than guarantee what a future trade will do.
pastTradeFaq.q9: Can beginners use Past Trade Analyzer?
pastTradeFaq.a9: Yes. It can help newer traders understand what happened in a completed trade and learn concepts such as market structure, entry timing, risk/reward, and stop-loss placement.
pastTradeFaq.a10: Yes. Experienced traders can use it as an additional review layer for checking execution quality and identifying recurring weaknesses or patterns.
pastTradeFaq.q11: Is a losing trade always a bad trade?
pastTradeFaq.a11: Not necessarily. A trade can follow a well-defined process and still lose because markets are uncertain. Reviewing the quality of the decision and execution can therefore be more useful than judging the trade only by its profit or loss.
pastTradeFaq.q12: Is a winning trade always a good trade?
pastTradeFaq.a12: Not necessarily. A profitable outcome does not automatically mean the entry, risk management, or execution was optimal. Reviewing the process helps separate outcome from decision quality.
pastTradeFaq.q13: Does the analyzer guarantee better trading results?
pastTradeFaq.a13: No. AI analysis cannot guarantee improved profits or future trading performance. The feature is designed to provide analytical and educational feedback.
pastTradeFaq.q14: How can I use the analyzer as part of my trading routine?
pastTradeFaq.a14:
A simple workflow is:
Take Trade → Record Trade → Analyze Trade → Identify Lessons → Update Your Process
Regular review can help turn your trading history into a continuous learning loop.
pastTradeFaq.q15: Is my trade analysis financial advice?
pastTradeFaq.a15: No. The analyzer should be treated as an analytical and educational tool. Trading involves substantial financial risk, and users remain responsible for their own trading decisions and risk management.
